title: DIRECTOR OF PUBLIC POLICY
description:
Houston Parks Board’s (HPB) mission is to expand, improve, and protect parks and greenspace in the Houston region. Since 1976, the 501(c)(3) not-for-profit organization has utilized public-private partnerships and its extensive philanthropic, government, and community relationships to create an interconnected network of parks, trails, and greenspace for a more resilient and equitable Houston region.


For 50 years, Houston Parks Board has partnered with the government and philanthropic leaders to expand, improve, and steward Houston's park system. Over the last decade, Bayou Greenways created the nation's largest connected urban trail network, investing more than $250 million and adding over 150 miles of trails and greenspaces that now connect neighborhoods, improve mobility, strengthen resilience, and serve nearly four million users annually.


Building on this trajectory, Houston Parks Board has embarked on an ambitious strategic plan. The plan calls for expanding beyond our current greenways to strengthen connectivity, reimagining 25 neighborhood parks, creating world-class regional destinations, and ensuring Houston's park system continues to meet the needs of one of America's fastest growing and most diverse cities. To achieve these goals, Houston Parks Board will need to raise its profile, ensure our communities prioritize investments in greenspace and convene partners to amplify our collective voices.


More information on Houston Parks Board and its initiatives is available at: .


POSITION OVERVIEW:


Reporting to the President & CEO, the Director of Public Policy is responsible for developing and executing a public policy strategy to advance Houston Parks Board’s (HPB) mission to expand, improve and protect parks and greenspace in the Houston region.


As a key member of HPB’s strategic direction-setting, the Director works closely with the CEO and the HPB executive team to develop and implement the organization’s strategy, a key component of which is engaging with public-sector partners to advance HPB’s mission. This role is focused on systemic policy advancement – building support for the Houston region’s park priorities among elected officials, activating community support, and maintaining and expanding HPB’s positive relationships with local, state, and federal government entities. The Director is expected to provide both strategic leadership and tactical execution to transform HPB’s project-based successes into long-term, systemic civic impact.


KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Develop a comprehensive public policy strategy that advances HPB’s mission through research, policy development, issue advocacy, and engagement of stakeholders including the general public, elected officials and coalition development of greenspace non-profits.
  • Monitor and analyze local, state, and federal legislation to identify opportunities or threats to HPB’s work and strategic plan as well as broader park and land use legislation.
  • Lead the development of policy briefs and technical analyses that translate HPB and sector data into compelling narratives for stakeholders.
  • Track and develop strategies around systemic issues such as public park funding, recurring maintenance needs and collaboration across regional partners.
  • Partner with the CEO and HPB leadership to refine frameworks for public and public-sector engagement.
  • Serve as a liaison between HPB and key external partners at the City of Houston, Harris County, other local governmental entities (e.g., TIRZs, Management Districts, Harris County Flood Control District) and state/federal agencies.
  • Support the President & CEO in engaging the Board of Directors by providing updates on the public policy landscape and the status of public-sector partnerships.
  • Work closely with the Communications and Development teams to ensure that public policy efforts reinforce fundraising strategies and public branding.
  • Work to convene other greenspace groups and non-profits to ensure coordination across the greenspace ecosystem and develop shared strategies.
  • Represent HPB at certain public events, including conferences, community forums and governmental entity public meetings to advance the organization’s strategic priorities.
  • Coordinate with the Projects, Development and Communications teams to translate public policy work into actionable strategies.

title: Senior C# Developer
description:
THE COMPANY

Lumion is redefining how architecture is communicated in the era of AI, from early concepts to final presentations. Our expanding portfolio helps architects, designers, and visualisation professionals communicate ideas with speed, clarity, and emotion, while making it easier for teams and stakeholders to collaborate around design.

We’re a passionate, international team of developers, designers, architects, and visualisation specialists looking to define how the AEC space collaborates on bringing design concepts to life. With a team across our Netherlands HQ, Denmark, Poland and a globally distributed remote workforce, we are at an exciting inflection point: new leadership, a growing product portfolio, and a market being rapidly reshaped by AI. The convergence of 3D rendering, real-time engines, and generative AI is accelerating, and we intend to lead it.

THE ROLE

We are seeking a Senior C# Engineer to join our team and serve as a foundational architect for our C# development environment. Working alongside our lead C# engineer, you will focus on evolving our scripting layer, transforming it into a high-performance, first-class citizen within the Lumion engine. You will play a pivotal role in defining the developer experience, performance characteristics, and long-term stability of the environment. You will drive the architecture from the ground up, designing the interop layer and API generators that bridge our native C++ core with a modern, idiomatic C# API. From memory management and serialization, you will help co-drive the technical roadmap that makes C# the premier environment for our developers.

WHAT YOU BRING

  • A proven track record in designing C# environment architectures for high-performance applications, with deep expertise in .NET 8/9+ and low-allocation hot paths.

  • A strong history of advocating for C# developer productivity, creating tools and APIs that prioritize ergonomics without sacrificing engine-level performance.

  • The ability to work collaboratively within the C# team, helping to shape and execute the vision for the C# scripting environment from concept to production-ready deployment.

CORE COMPETENCIES

  • API Design: Ability to create "idiomatic" C# interfaces that hide native complexity without sacrificing performance.

  • Performance Profiling: Ability to use tools to identify bottlenecks in C# code and interop overhead.

  • Compiler & Tooling Knowledge: Experience with Roslyn or similar build-time analysis tools is a major plus.

YOU’LL THRIVE HERE IF

  • You enjoy "peeling the onion"—deconstructing complex, legacy systems and rebuilding them into clean, modern architectures.

  • You value "Process, Not Outcome"—you appreciate technical depth and enjoy documenting the "why" behind design decisions.

  • You are comfortable working in a hybrid environment where you influence both the low-level native engine code and the high-level application logic.

  • You want to define the future of AEC software, where 3D rendering, real-time engines, and generative AI converge.

title: Pricing Director (m/f/d)
description:
About the role:

As Director, Pricing, you will define and lead the pricing strategy for Redcare Pharmacy’s retail business, operating at the intersection of commercial strategy, advanced analytics and technology. Your primary mandate is to continuously improve how we price products and transactions, balancing profitability, revenue and customer price competitiveness at significant e-commerce scale.

You will set the direction for an even more scientific, dynamic and data-driven pricing approach and ensure that pricing decisions translate into measurable business impact. Beyond our core retail platform, your scope will also extend to the further development of marketplace and own-brand pricing.

The role has a broad strategic stakeholder landscape. You will work closely with senior leaders across Category Management and Country Management, as well as Data & AI, Controlling, Marketing and Procurement. You will also partner with Tech and Product teams responsible for our webshop and underlying capabilities, ensuring that pricing strategy, data and technology evolve together.

About your tasks:

  • Own and advance our core retail pricing strategy: Define how Redcare Pharmacy approaches pricing across its e-commerce platform, balancing profitability, revenue and price competitiveness and translating strategic priorities into measurable commercial outcomes.

  • Build a scientific and dynamic pricing approach: Raise the analytical standard of pricing through robust experimentation, A/B testing, modelling and validation. Establish clear methodologies for understanding causality and measuring the incremental impact generated by pricing decisions.

  • Drive pricing at scale: Develop the frameworks and decision logic required for increasingly dynamic, real-time pricing, ensuring our approach can respond effectively to customer behavior, competitive movements and changing commercial conditions.

  • Shape decisions across the business: Establish pricing as a key input into decision-making across Commercial, Controlling, Procurement Tech and Product, aligning stakeholders around the trade-offs and opportunities behind pricing decisions.

  • Set the direction for the Pricing function: Lead and develop a growing team of 9+ pricing professionals, set a high analytical bar and represent pricing with senior leadership and the Board.

About you:

  • You bring 10+ years of relevant professional experience, with deep expertise in B2C e-commerce pricing and at least 3 years in a leadership role. You have worked with digital commerce products at significant scale, ideally in an environment comparable to Redcare Pharmacy’s 14.5 million active users.

  • You combine strategic thinking with deep analytical and quantitative expertise. A strong background in mathematics, analytics, data science or related discipline enables you to challenge methodologies, understand the underlying data and confidently assess the validity of pricing experiments.

  • You understand dynamic pricing in high-volume e-commerce environments and are comfortable with pricing that changes in real time. You can demonstrate how sophisticated pricing strategies, experimentation and analytical models have translated into measurable improvements in profitability, revenue and/or customer price competitiveness.

  • You have the seniority to influence a broad cross-functional stakeholder landscape, both across business functions and at Managing Board level, while remaining sufficiently close to the analytical detail to challenge your team and communicate pricing decisions at Board level.

title: Project Manager
description:
Project Manager

Warehouse Fit-out/Installation

Site Based – Travel throughout Europe


Who are we:

We are a global provider of Installation (M&E), Integration, and Fit-out services, delivering end-to-end workplace transformation projects across Europe. Our Warehouse Fit-out team specialises in converting empty building envelopes into fully operational facilities, covering new builds, expansions, and retrofits. From facility fit-outs and workstation construction to IT infrastructure, material deployment, and strategic safety installations, we provide turnkey solutions for commercial and industrial clients. Our mission is to empower our customers to excel through innovative, tailored design and installation solutions, driven by our commitment to Flawless Execution.


About the Role:

We are looking for an accomplished Project Manager to join our Warehouse Fit-out delivery team and take full responsibility for the successful delivery of large-scale facility fit-out projects throughout Europe. Reporting to a Senior Project Manager, you will be involved at every stage, from initial feasibility through detailed planning, physical build-out, snagging, and handover, ensuring each project is executed to the highest standard. The work encompasses the full scope of warehouse and industrial facility transformation, including structural modifications, workstation installations, IT and data cabling, mechanical and electrical services coordination, and health and safety infrastructure.

You will maintain a comprehensive understanding of every project you lead, balancing the bigger picture with a hands-on grasp of the construction detail, while driving accountability across internal teams, subcontractors, and supply chain partners. Client relationships sit at the heart of this role; you will be the face of the business on site, building trust with key stakeholders and identifying opportunities to add value beyond the core scope. Commercially sharp and delivery-focused, you will manage project budgets with precision, protect margin, and ensure every decision is made with both the client outcome and business performance in mind.

title: Associate, Risk & Reporting
description:
About Oaktree

Oaktree is a leader among global investment managers specializing in alternative investments, with more than $220 billion in assets under management. The firm emphasizes an opportunistic, value-oriented, and risk-controlled approach to investments in credit, equity, and real estate. The firm has more than 1,400 employees and offices in more than 25 cities worldwide.

We are committed to cultivating an environment that is collaborative, curious, inclusive and honors diversity of thought. Providing training and career development opportunities and emphasizing strong support for our local communities through philanthropic initiatives are essential to our culture.

For additional information, please visit Oaktree’s website at

The Risk & Reporting (R&R) team delivers best-in-class, technology-enabled performance analytics and investor reporting for Oaktree's closed-end, open-end and evergreen strategies - including Private Credit, Opportunistic Credit, Asset-Backed Finance, Special Situations, Real Estate and other R&R-supported strategies. The team works at the intersection of investments, finance / accounting, client reporting, and technology, partnering with deal teams, Investor Relations / Client Services, Finance / Accounting, Valuation, Data Management, IT, and Legal / Compliance to ensure performance, exposure, allocation, and client-reporting data is accurate, validated, and ready for investor and portfolio-management use.
As an Assistant Vice President, you will manage a coverage area within the R&R reporting platform, review and approve key deliverables, set operating standards, manage senior-stakeholder expectations, and use hands-on people management to build a high-performing Hyderabad team.
What You'll Do
Performance & Reporting
• Manage quality standards for strategy- and investment-level track records - TWR, MWR, IRR (gross and net), MOIC, TVPI, DPI, and RVPI - across Oaktree's closed-end, open-end and evergreen strategies;
• Review and approve investment-level performance outputs across deployments, valuation changes, realizations, exits, distributions, exposure movements, and return drivers, ensuring metrics tie to approved source reports, position-level extracts, and investment-performance summaries;
• Oversee reporting workflows across R&R-supported strategies, including strategy and portfolio summaries, investment performance summaries, exposure and attribution reports, client-specific templates, meeting packs, and ad hoc requests;
• Oversee bespoke client template validation, including exposure-by-GICS reports, BIS / Basel and ILPA-style templates, instrument classifications, issuer and underlying-asset details, fair-value exceptions, trade / maturity fields, and bank-loan, CLO, and derivative economics;
• Set review standards for benchmark and PME analyses where relevant, using vintage-year peer benchmarks and indices such as Cliffwater, MSCI/Burgiss, Cambridge Associates, and Preqin;
• Manage quarterly fair-value and valuation reporting controls so marks and exposure data flow accurately into performance outputs; and
• Guide review of portfolio analytics such as loss, default, recovery, watchlist, leverage, yield, sector, geography, and currency exposure metrics across private-credit and opportunistic-credit portfolios.
Investor Reporting
• Manage delivery standards for investor-reporting data packs, RFP / DDQ inputs, capital-account and transaction schedules, and standardized LP reporting using ILPA templates such as Reporting, Capital Call & Distribution, and Performance templates;
• Review and approve investment-level data controls across Finance / Accounting, Valuation, Data Management, and internal reporting systems, ensuring values tie to approved source reports, investment-performance summaries, position files, and client-template requirements;
• Manage controlled LP, consultant, and internal investor-reporting request trackers, including ownership, service levels, escalation paths, audit trails, and recurring monthly / quarterly task visibility; and
• Oversee LP performance summaries, portfolio and financial data packages, investment-level cash-flow templates, and investor-specific reporting packs, including side-letter, parallel-fund, eFront, and exclusion-list requirements.
Technology & Automation
• Manage automation priorities across SQL, Python, Power BI, Microsoft Fabric, and paginated-report workflows, focusing on scale, control, and production resilience;
• Set standards for use of Oaktree's in-house systems and reporting datasets, including repeatable sourcing, break investigation, and data-quality controls;
• Review semantic-model-ready reporting assets in Microsoft Fabric and Power BI, including DAX measures, Power Query / M transformations, Fabric dataflows, deployment-pipeline support, and secure data-access controls; and
• Coach the team on product discipline - documentation, testing, version control, release management, and clear handoffs - while using approved GenAI tooling responsibly.
Partnership & Leadership
• Manage relationships with Portfolio Management and deal teams, Business Development, Product Specialists, Investor Relations / Client Services, Finance / Accounting, Valuation, Data Management, IT, and Legal / Compliance for assigned R&R workstreams;
• Set priorities for strategy and portfolio reporting enhancements in response to new strategies, investor requests, control needs, and ILPA-aligned reporting expectations;
• Manage team capacity, review quality, deadlines, escalations, onboarding, feedback, and development for analysts, associates, and senior associates, with a focus on building a high-performing team.

Required
• 10+ years at an asset management firm, investment bank, fund administrator, or other financial services company, with deep exposure to alternative investments, investment reporting, or portfolio analytics;
• Deep knowledge of return and performance concepts, including TWR, MWR, IRR, MOIC, TVPI, DPI, RVPI, exposure, attribution, benchmark, and investor-reporting outputs across closed-end, open-end or evergreen strategies;
• Strong technical foundation in SQL, Python, Power BI, and modern reporting platforms, with experience setting standards for recurring production workflows;
• Demonstrated people-management experience building high-performing teams, quality review discipline, cross-functional project leadership, and senior-stakeholder management, with outstanding written and verbal communication skills.
Preferred
• Hands-on Python for data analysis and automation, and prompt engineering using approved GenAI tools;
• Familiarity with cloud data architectures and tooling such as Azure or Microsoft Fabric, semantic models, deployment pipelines, and secure data-access patterns;
• Working knowledge of alternative-investment accounting concepts, investor-platform or eFront-style workflows, side-letter data requirements, and ILPA reporting standards;
• Familiarity with project management tools such as Jira and Confluence.
How You Work
• Outstanding initiative and the ability to operate independently on short- and long-term goals, with a strong work ethic;
• A builder's mindset - energized by automating manual processes and shipping durable, well-engineered analytical tools;
• Curious, rigorous, and intellectually honest, with the patience to work through complex, time-sensitive data until the numbers and narrative hold together;
• Excellent interpersonal skills and the ability to manage stakeholders, escalations, and cross-functional priorities effectively;
• Organized and able to manage team capacity, review cycles, deadlines, and competing priorities;
• Team-oriented, with strong integrity and professionalism, and the ability to develop analysts, associates, and senior associates into a high-performing team through change.
Education & Credentials
Bachelor's degree required. Industry-relevant professional credentials are a strong plus, including the CFA, FRM, CAIA, and CIPM designations, and/or a Chartered Accountant (CA) qualification.

Overview

The program coordinator is responsible for program coordination of four grant-funded programs. The CUPO Office is home to four grants; The Collegiate Science & Technology Entry Program (CSTEP) funded through New York State Department of Education, The Ronald E. McNair Post-Baccalaureate Achievement Program (McNair) a United States Department of Education TRIO Program, and The Louis Stokes Alliances for Minority Participation Program (LSAMP) funded by the National Science Foundation. The fourth program is the NYSED STEP Program: IMPETUS for Career Success.

For CUPO and IMPETUS the program coordinator will facilitate program activities, coordinate on and off campus events and organize logistics, collect and maintain student data in order to conform to grant regulations and reporting. Coordinator will collaborate with program directors and partners to address any concerns or improvements to help the program thrive.

Strong interpersonal, organizational and communication skills. Sensitivity to the needs of culturally diverse and disadvantaged students. Willingness to work occasional weekends and evening commitments.
